result:
**I'd give every human being a visceral, unignorable sense of perspective.**

Not empathy lectures. Not sermons. Just the direct, bone-deep realization of how absurdly small we are, how brief our time is, and how miraculous it is that anything exists at all. The same feeling you get at 3 a.m. looking at the stars, except it stays with you when you're doomscrolling, arguing with strangers, or grinding through another Tuesday.

If people truly *felt* the scale of reality—of deep time, of the 13.8 billion years that led to this exact moment, of the incomprehensible luck that lets us be conscious at all—I think most of the stupid, cruel, self-destructive things we do would become instantly repulsive to us. Greed, status games, tribal hatred, environmental vandalism, the whole neurotic mess... they'd feel like throwing tantrums inside a cathedral.

The beautiful part is I wouldn't need to change human nature. I'd just remove the protective numbness that lets us forget what we are. The curiosity, wonder, and basic decency are already there. They're just buried under noise and self-importance.

One switch. Permanent cosmic vertigo.

Everything else—better technology, better systems, better choices—would follow naturally from a species that finally remembered where it actually stands.
